messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on canary around 02:10 UTC. latency tail jumped. rolling back?
kevin: @maria can you paste the perf profile + a sample request that missed?
maria: attaching quick summary: overall hit-rate went from 78% -> 66% for the cohort serving /chat endpoints. Most misses are short system-prompt-heavy requests.
ashok: any recent changes to canonicalization or tokenizer pinning?
maria: yes — last deploy included a small prompt sanitization change that trims trailing whitespace from user messages, and we switched the tokenizer pin to v3.1 for canary.
olivia: trimming whitespace should only increase hits normally. token pin can change tokenization boundaries though, so cache keys can diverge.
jing: perf-bot ran a microprofile, here's the hot path: kernel selection shifted to cuBLAS path more often due to seq_len histogram bump (avg seq up 8%). KV lookup cost is similar but misses amplify token-gen work.
perf-bot: profile summary attached in thread (short):
```
top consumes: kv_lookup (10%), kernel_launch (42%), softmax (12%), kv_build (8%)
seq_len_p50: 88 -> 95
cache_hit_rate: 78% -> 66%
most-missed-prefix: "SYSTEM: You are an assistant..." (variants)
```
kevin: interesting — system prompt variants. Did sanitization change system prompt formatting?
maria: we only changed user-side trim, but our system prompt template has a conditional that inserts a trailing newline for v2 models. That was toggled in the same deploy for compatibility. Could be two small diffs compounding.
ashok: so hypothesis: tokenizer pin v3.1 + newline toggle -> canonicalized bytes differ -> cache key mismatch -> demolish hit-rate.
olivia: can we reproduce with a deterministic sample? maria, can you dump tokenizer tokens for the failing requests using both pins?
maria: yes. sample pair below:
```
original_user: "Translate to French: Hello world  "
tokenizer-v2: [50256, 100, 215, 12]
tokenizer-v3.1: [50256, 100, 215, 12]  // same for user part
system prompt v2 (no newline): tokens...
system prompt v2 (with newline): adds token 198 (newline) between system and user -> cache key mismatch
```
jing: aha — even one extra token in system prompt shifts the whole probe sig. KV prefix matching is exact currently (byte/token-level). small insertion -> miss.
kevin: two options: 1) make cache key tolerant to trailing whitespace/newline in system prompt (normalize), 2) pin tokenizer consistently across rolling deploys, 3) add a best-effort prefix fuzzy-match for short system prompts. tradeoffs?
ashok: fuzzy-match is risky for correctness. I'd prefer deterministic normalization + stronger deploy gating to ensure tokenizer pin doesn't flip unexpectedly.
olivia: agree. normalization seems low-risk: strip trailing newlines in system prompt before keying, collapse consecutive spaces, and canonicalize tool/function-call fields ordering.
maria: note: toolcall fields order also caused misses in 3 customer repros — the tool metadata map gets serialized in insertion order currently. We should stable-sort keys before hashing.
kevin: add to checklist: (a) canonicalize system prompt (strip trailing whitespace/newline, collapse repeated spaces), (b) stable-serialize tool metadata (sorted keys), (c) require tokenizer pin compatibility in rollout config.
jing: i'll run a simulation over last 24h logs to estimate hit-rate improvement if we canonicalize. give me 30m.
ashok: also check kernel selection interplay — if seq_len shifts and we pick heavier kernels but have lower cache hit, unit cost spikes. we should add hit-rate to autoscaler signals so burst capacity accounts for cache miss inflation.
maria: rolling back the newline toggle on canary now. deploy-bot: rolling back canary: model-runtime toggle -> previous (no newline) at 2460123459 :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary rollback complete at 2460123461 :rocket:
kevin: good. keep the canary at previous behavior while we run the simulation. jing, ping when you have numbers.
jing: quick sim done — canonicalization (system prompt trim + sorted tool keys) projects hit-rate recovery from 66% -> ~75% (not full 78%, tokenizer pin accounts for remainder).
olivia: that matches expectation. tokenizer differences cause edge token boundary mismatches for few prompts. can we add a tokenization-compatibility check during deploys that compares sample corpus tokenization across pins and fails if >1% divergence?
kevin: yes. add to rollout gate: tokenization divergence check + small unit test on canonicalized cache key equality.
maria: I'll open a PR with canonicalization patch (small util in runtime cache keying) and a deploy-gate change. PR will include a reproducible script and sample logs.
nashok: also document the threat model: any system prompt change needs cache-key migration plan (either force flush or remap old keys).
kevin: question: do we want to invalidate cache on system-prompt formatting change automatically for Dedicated customers? that could be costly.
olivia: default should be no auto flush; instead emit an alert and recommend scheduled warmup. But for major security-critical system prompt changes maybe auto-invalidate via policy flag.
maria: PR linked when ready. I'll include test vectors and a small perf run showing kernel selection impact pre/post change.
jing: final note: we should add a lightweight prefix signature that is tokenizer-version-agnostic: e.g., use normalized unicode + sha1 of collapsed text as a secondary index to allow fallback matches within short window. but that's extra infra.
kevin: file follow-ups: 1) canonicalize impl PR, 2) rollout gate PR, 3) logging metric for token-pin diffs, 4) postmortem if rollback hadn't been quick. thanks everyone.
olivia: :thumbsup:
